purpose: Vincristine is a chemotherapy medicine used to treat certain types of cancer, including leukemia, lymphoma, and other cancers. It is often given along with other cancer medicines as part of a treatment plan. Your doctor has chosen it because it is effective at stopping cancer cells from growing and spreading.
how_it_works: Vincristine works by interfering with the way cancer cells divide and multiply. It blocks a process inside the cell that is needed to pull the cell apart when it tries to split into two new cells. Because cancer cells divide very quickly, this medicine is especially good at targeting them and stopping them from growing.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include numbness, tingling, or pain in your hands and feet (called neuropathy), constipation, stomach cramps, weakness in your muscles, hair loss, and mouth sores. You may also feel tired or have a decreased appetite. Let your care team know right away if any of these bother you.
warnings: Vincristine must NEVER be given as a spinal injection — it is only given into a vein (IV), and giving it any other way can be fatal. It can cause serious nerve damage, so tell your doctor right away if you notice increasing numbness, weakness, or pain. It can also cause severe constipation or bowel problems, so staying hydrated and following your doctor's advice about stool softeners is very important. Avoid contact with people who are sick, as this medicine can lower your ability to fight infections.
typical_dosing: Vincristine is given by a nurse or doctor directly into your vein (IV) — you will not take this at home as a pill. The dose depends on your body size, the type of cancer being treated, and the specific treatment plan your doctor has chosen. It is usually given once a week or on a schedule set by your cancer care team. Always follow your oncologist's instructions exactly.
